result.summary:
Implemented all five items of review-test-followup-r01.md as a unified diff against docs/validation/evidence/starter-integration-planning-2026-09-20/candidate-test_starter_structures.gd only. No production source, no full test-file rewrite, and no other file was touched, matching the sole allowed patch path.

Item 1 (executable reference-loading): appended `test_frozen_layout_reference_matches_the_literal_oracle`, following the repository's own FileAccess.get_file_as_string + JSON.parse_string pattern from test_save_section_component_columns.gd. It guards file existence, successful read, Dictionary parse, and the seven expected top-level keys (returning early on any guard failure so a missing/malformed reference is an explicit failure, never silently skipped), then cross-checks: all 31 floor_furniture entries (symbol mapped through a new FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY table to key/origin/room/footprint/candidate_walk_tiles) against FURNITURE_ORACLE; the 7 solid_partition_edges plus the 1 door_edge, merged and sorted by tile_a, against EDGE_ORACLE's tile pairs and kinds; exit_interior_tile against EXIT_INTERIOR_LOCAL; and walk_tiles/reachable_walk_tiles both against each other and against an 80-minus-this-oracle's-own-footprints set independently recomputed in the test itself. Building/room/header values, which the JSON does not carry, are explicitly left as the existing contract literals, per the instruction. The suite's top doc comment is rewritten to say the reference is now loaded and checked, not merely transcribed.

Item 2: added `test_same_producer_two_outputs_do_not_alias`, using one producer to prepare two separate Plan outputs, mutating one entry in each of A's ten arrays and proving B's snapshot is untouched, then mutating one entry in each of B's ten arrays and proving A's (already-dirtied) snapshot is untouched.

Item 3: replaced the literal-constant tautology (`assert_true(1 != 2 and 2 != 4 and 3 != 6, ...)`) in `test_room_ordinals_are_not_the_protected_room_type_ids` with a loop that reads `plan.room_field(ordinal, ROOM_COL_TYPE_ID)` for ordinals 1..3 and asserts each actual stored value differs from its own ordinal.

Item 4: corrected the wall-interior witness in `test_exit_wall_gates` from global (64,67) -- which was literally the exit's own interior tile -- to global (64,66), a genuinely different interior tile, keeping the same expected STARTER_EXIT_WALL code.

Item 5: converted `test_walk_disconnected_sole_door_replaced` into `test_walk_disconnected_gates`, retaining the sole-door-replaced case verbatim and adding a second case that drifts the header's walk_tile_count (47 -> 46) with everything else authored-correct, both expecting STARTER_WALK_DISCONNECTED. Also retained explicit out-of-range candidate-VALUE coverage (2147483647, one of the two literal values the instruction names) as a distinct case alongside -- not replacing -- the existing coherent-compacted-arena missing-neighbour case in `test_access_candidate_gates`.

Every removed/old hunk line is transcribed character-for-character from the provided current candidate file content in this dispatch. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this environment gives me no diff/patch tool and no file line numbers; the `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` line numbers in the hunks below are my own best-effort manual count through the ~718-line file and may be off by a few lines, though I recounted the added/context line totals in each hunk's own body to keep each hunk's internal `-`/`+` line counts self-consistent. The context and changed text themselves are exact matches to the file as given, so a human or a fuzzy-matching patch tool (e.g. `patch`, or `git apply --recount`) should still locate and apply each hunk correctly even if a line-number offset is imperfect; a strict-mode `git apply` with no fuzz tolerance may need line-number correction first, which I cannot verify without execution. I have not run this diff, git apply, or the resulting suite; no pass/fail claim is made.

 func test_extreme_and_out_of_range_values_refuse_without_crashing() -> void:
 	var cases: Array = [
 		_case("building origin at int64 max wraps into an invalid int32 tile", func(p): p.set_building_field(0, PlanClass.BUILDING_COL_GLOBAL_ORIGIN_TILE, 9223372036854775807), StarterStructures.REFUSE_BUILDING_LAYOUT),

+# --- frozen layout-reference.json cross-check (review-test-followup-r01 item 1) ------------------
+
+const LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH: String = \
+	"res://../docs/validation/evidence/starter-integration-planning-2026-09-20/layout-reference.json"
+
+const FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY: Dictionary = {
+	"B": "bed", "K": "kitchen_bench", "H": "hearth", "T": "seat", "S": "shelf",
+}
+
+
+func _to_int_array(values: Array) -> Array:
+	"""Coerce a JSON-parsed numeric Array (floats) into an Array of ints for comparison."""
+	var out: Array = []
+	for v in values:
+		out.append(int(v))
+	return out
+
+
+func test_frozen_layout_reference_matches_the_literal_oracle() -> void:
+	"""Executable reference consistency: load the frozen JSON this suite's literal oracle
+	constants were transcribed from, guard its existence/parse/shape, and cross-check it against
+	FURNITURE_ORACLE/EDGE_ORACLE/EXIT_INTERIOR_LOCAL. Building/room/header values are not carried
+	by the JSON and remain explicit contract literals, per review-test-followup-r01.md item 1."""
+	assert_true(FileAccess.file_exists(LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH), "layout-reference.json must exist")
+	if not FileAccess.file_exists(LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH):
+		return
+	var raw: String = FileAccess.get_file_as_string(LAYOUT_REFERENCE_PATH)
+	assert_false(raw.is_empty(), "layout-reference.json must be readable")
+	if raw.is_empty():
+		return
+	var parsed: Variant = JSON.parse_string(raw)
+	assert_true(parsed is Dictionary, "layout-reference.json must parse to a Dictionary")
+	if not (parsed is Dictionary):
+		return
+	var reference: Dictionary = parsed
+	var required_keys: Array = ["floor_furniture", "solid_partition_edges", "door_edge",
+		"exit_interior_tile", "walk_tiles", "reachable_walk_tiles", "diagram"]
+	for key in required_keys:
+		assert_true(reference.has(key), "layout-reference.json must carry '%s'" % key)
+		if not reference.has(key):
+			return
+
+	var loaded_furniture: Array = reference["floor_furniture"]
+	assert_equal(loaded_furniture.size(), FURNITURE_ORACLE.size(), "furniture entry count agrees with the reference")
+	for row in range(mini(loaded_furniture.size(), FURNITURE_ORACLE.size())):
+		var loaded: Dictionary = loaded_furniture[row]
+		var expected: Dictionary = FURNITURE_ORACLE[row]
+		var symbol: String = String(loaded["symbol"])
+		assert_true(FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY.has(symbol), "reference furniture %d has a known symbol" % row)
+		assert_equal(FURNITURE_SYMBOL_KEY.get(symbol, ""), expected["key"], "reference furniture %d key" % row)
+		assert_equal(int(loaded["origin"]), int(expected["origin"]), "reference furniture %d origin" % row)
+		assert_equal(int(loaded["room"]), int(expected["room"]), "reference furniture %d room" % row)
+		assert_equal(_to_int_array(loaded["footprint"]), expected["footprint"], "reference furniture %d footprint" % row)
+		assert_equal(_to_int_array(loaded["candidate_walk_tiles"]), expected["candidates"], "reference furniture %d candidates" % row)
+
+	var loaded_partitions: Array = reference["solid_partition_edges"]
+	var loaded_door: Array = reference["door_edge"]
+	assert_equal(loaded_partitions.size() + 1, EDGE_ORACLE.size(), "partition + door edge count agrees with the reference")
+	var reference_edges: Array = []
+	for pair in loaded_partitions:
+		reference_edges.append([int(pair[0]), int(pair[1]), "interior_partition"])
+	reference_edges.append([int(loaded_door[0]), int(loaded_door[1]), "interior_door"])
+	reference_edges.sort_custom(func(a, b): return a[0] < b[0])
+	for row in range(mini(reference_edges.size(), EDGE_ORACLE.size())):
+		var loaded_edge: Array = reference_edges[row]
+		var expected_edge: Dictionary = EDGE_ORACLE[row]
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[0], expected_edge["a"], "reference edge %d tile_a" % row)
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[1], expected_edge["b"], "reference edge %d tile_b" % row)
+		assert_equal(loaded_edge[2], expected_edge["kind"], "reference edge %d kind" % row)
+
+	assert_equal(int(reference["exit_interior_tile"]), EXIT_INTERIOR_LOCAL, "reference exit interior tile agrees with the literal oracle")
+
+	var loaded_walk: Array = reference["walk_tiles"]
+	var loaded_reachable: Array = reference["reachable_walk_tiles"]
+	assert_equal(_to_int_array(loaded_walk), _to_int_array(loaded_reachable), "reference walk_tiles and reachable_walk_tiles agree with each other")
+	assert_equal(loaded_walk.size(), 47, "reference walk tile count matches the contract's 47")
+
+	var occupied: Dictionary = {}
+	for entry in FURNITURE_ORACLE:
+		for tile in entry["footprint"]:
+			occupied[int(tile)] = true
+	var walk_from_oracle: Array = []
+	for local in 80:
+		if not occupied.has(local):
+			walk_from_oracle.append(local)
+	assert_equal(_to_int_array(loaded_walk), walk_from_oracle, "reference walk tiles equal 80 interior tiles minus this oracle's own footprints")
+
+
+# --- same-producer, two-output non-aliasing (review-test-followup-r01 item 2) ---------------------
+
+func test_same_producer_two_outputs_do_not_alias() -> void:
+	var producer := StarterStructures.new()
+	var plan_a := StarterStructures.Plan.new()
+	var plan_b := StarterStructures.Plan.new()
+	assert_true(producer.prepare_into(plan_a), "first output prepares")
+	assert_true(producer.prepare_into(plan_b), "second output from the same producer prepares")
+	var snapshot_b := _snapshot_plan(plan_b)
+
+	plan_a.buildings[0] = 111
+	plan_a.rooms[0] = 111
+	plan_a.room_tiles[0] = 111
+	plan_a.furniture[0] = 111
+	plan_a.footprints[0] = 111
+	plan_a.candidate_access_tiles[0] = 111
+	plan_a.edges[0] = 111
+	plan_a.exit_tiles[0] = 111
+	plan_a.bed_furniture_ordinals[0] = 111
+	plan_a.header[0] = 111
+	_assert_plan_matches_snapshot(plan_b, snapshot_b, "mutating A must not alias B")
+
+	var snapshot_a := _snapshot_plan(plan_a)
+	plan_b.buildings[0] = 222
+	plan_b.rooms[0] = 222
+	plan_b.room_tiles[0] = 222
+	plan_b.furniture[0] = 222
+	plan_b.footprints[0] = 222
+	plan_b.candidate_access_tiles[0] = 222
+	plan_b.edges[0] = 222
+	plan_b.exit_tiles[0] = 222
+	plan_b.bed_furniture_ordinals[0] = 222
+	plan_b.header[0] = 222
+	_assert_plan_matches_snapshot(plan_a, snapshot_a, "mutating B must not alias A")
